title: product-prd-unified-inference-product-overview-roadmap-pricing-release-2028-06-15
author: Priya Patel
summary: This document consolidates the product overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap themes, pricing & packaging notes, and the release notes for the Unified Inference product line (hosted, Dedicated, Private). It is intended for cross-functional stakeholders: product, engineering, sales, and customer success.
background: Redwood's Unified Inference product provides a single developer-facing API and operational surface for hosted inference, reserved/dedicated capacity, and private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Over the last 24 months the product has focused on reliability and cost controls; this PRD defines the next phase to (1) simplify pricing and packaging for mid-market customers, (2) introduce predictable latency SLAs for Dedicated customers, and (3) deliver a v2 of routing and fallback logic to reduce P99 tail latency.
goals:
- Deliver a unified, easy-to-explain product story that maps to customer needs (self-serve, reserved, private).
- Ship feature set required for Q3 sales plays: SLA-backed Dedicated tiers, private deployment automation, and volume-pricing incentives.
- Improve observable cost-per-token by 15% through Optimize-driven recommendations and enhanced caching.
- Reduce customer-reported latency incidents by 40% via routing improvements and model-variant fallbacks.
non_goals:
- Replace underlying runtime or GPU scheduler (this PRD assumes current runtime/kernel improvements are in parallel projects).
- End-to-end migration tooling for customers on competitor platforms (out of scope; we'll provide migration guidance but not one-click migration in this release).
user_personas:
- Product/engineering teams at mid-market SaaS companies who need predictable cost and SLAs.
- Platform teams managing internal LLM features (A/B tests, rollouts).
- Security/compliance leads evaluating Private deployment options for regulated data.
requirements:
1) Unified API and SDK parity: text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming, and function/tool-calling must be available across Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
2) SLA-backed Dedicated tiers: define latency SLOs (P50 < 100ms, P95 < 300ms, P99 < 700ms for 8k-context baseline) and an uptime SLA (99.9% monthly).
3) Cost controls: add per-route batching configuration, automated caching suggestions, and per-token cost estimates in Console.
4) Routing & fallback v2: policy engine to route by latency/cost/region with automatic fallback to compatible quantized variants.
5) Private deployment automation: Terraform module + installer that supports KMS integration (AWS KMS/Azure KeyVault) and audit-log forwarding.
6) Observability: per-model, per-route dashboards for token-level cost, latency histograms, error rates, and rollout tracing hooks.
7) Pricing: simplified three-tier pricing (Developer, Business, Enterprise) with clear reserved capacity discounts and volume bands.
8) Security & compliance: default encryption-at-rest, RBAC controls in Console, and SOC2 evidence package updated.
9) Performance guardrails: default batching and sequence-length-based kernel selection enabled with opt-out flags.
10) Backwards compatibility: existing customer routes must continue to work; breaking changes must have a 90-day deprecation window.
acceptance_criteria:
- API parity: SDK tests (node/python/go) pass end-to-end on Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- SLA verification: synthetic SLO tests across three regions show compliance under 95th percentile load pattern.
- Pricing UI: Console shows per-route cost estimates and customer-facing pricing pages updated.
- Private installer: tested in two on-prem environments (air-gapped and VPC) with KMS integration and audit logs.
- Observability: dashboards accessible and instrumented for top 10 customer routes.
- Security: RBAC controls validated by internal security review and SOC2 audit checklist updated.
design_overview:
High-level design: the product exposes a single HTTP/SDK surface backed by a routing plane and the serving runtime. The routing plane enforces policies (latency-first, cost-first, region affinity) and rewrites requests for fallback variants when needed. The serving runtime manages model variants, quantized kernels, KV cache, and dynamic batching.

Key components:
- API Gateway (Redwood API): authentication, rate limits, initial request shaping.
- Routing Plane (Policy Engine): rules, fallback registry, model-variant compatibility matrix.
- Serving Runtime: model kernels, KV cache, batching orchestrator.
- Dedicated Manager: reserved pool allocator and autoscaling rules.
- Private Installer: terraform modules, operator tooling, and onboarding playbook.
- Console & Observability: dashboards, cost breakdowns, tracing, and rollouts UI.

Design decisions:
- Use model-variant compatibility matrix to avoid on-the-fly model transpilation.
- Prioritize prefix/KV caching for chat workloads; offer fine-grained cache controls per-route.
- Route control plane to be stateless; state kept in Redis-backed registry for fast lookups.
- Pricing decisions decoupled from routing to allow runtime cost signals without changing customer billing immediately.
architecture_diagram: (diagram) API Gateway -> Routing Plane -> Serving Runtime (KV cache, batching, kernels) -> GPU pools / Dedicated Manager. Private deployments run the same components behind a customer VPC with a private control plane. See internal drawing ID: arch-unified-inference-2028-06 for detailed sequence diagrams.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Beta, Weeks 0-4): Private pilot customers and Dedicated power users; runbook validation and observability tuning.
Phase 1 (GA for Hosted & Dedicated, Weeks 5-12): Enable new pricing tiers, SLA contracts available; gradual ramp via feature flags and canary routing.
Phase 2 (Private GA, Weeks 13-20): On-prem installer and privacy controls, sales enablement for enterprise.
Phase 3 (Post-GA, Weeks 21-32): Optimize recommendations (Redwood Optimize integrations) and open documentation for self-serve migrations.
Rollout steps:
1) Create canary routes (5 customers) for SLA-backed Dedicated.
2) Run synthetic SLO verification and load tests.
3) Open pricing for new customers; grandfather existing commitments with opt-in migration.
4) Expand to 25% traffic with automatic rollback policy on error budget breach.
5) Full GA after 4 weeks of stable metrics.
migration_and_compatibility:
- Existing customers: maintain current route IDs and model pins; provide migration guide with automated prompts in Console.
- Breaking changes: announced 90 days prior with migration scripts.
- SDKs: maintain semver and publish migration notes for any client-side changes.
- Model variants: runtime will support legacy non-quantized variants for at least 6 months after migration prompts.
metrics_and_success:
Primary metrics: monthly recurring revenue (MRR) from Dedicated seats, avg. cost-per-token, P99 latency, number of Private deployments, churn rate for high-usage customers.
Target success criteria (90 days post-GA):
- MRR from Dedicated increased by 22% vs baseline.
- Cost-per-token improved by 15% for customers using Optimize recommendations.
- P99 latency reduced by 40% for routes using routing+fallback v2.
- 5 private deployments completed with no critical security findings.
pricing_and_packaging:
Overview: three simplified tiers with clear triggers for Dedicated and Private.
Tiers:
- Developer (self-serve Hosted): pay-as-you-go per-token pricing, free quota (100k tokens/mo), no SLA, community support.
- Business (self-serve & sales-assist): volume discounts starting at 10M tokens/mo, optional reserved capacity add-on (10%-25% discount), email support, best-effort latency targets.
- Enterprise (sales-assisted): contract pricing, Dedicated reservations with SLA (99.9%), Private deployment options, advanced observability add-ons, 24/7 support.
Reserved capacity: monthly commitments with tiered discounts (see pricing bands: 0-50k GPU-hours, 50-250k, >250k).
Volume discounts: banded per-token discounts applied monthly.
Add-ons: advanced observability retention, compliance package (SOC2+, HIPAA), premium SLAs, and on-prem deployment support.
Billing and invoicing: billing calc remains usage-based with reserved capacity credits applied at invoice time; Finance will publish updated contract templates and SOWs.
release_notes_summary:
Release 2028.6 (GA):
- Unified API parity across Hosted, Dedicated, Private for text, chat, embeddings, streaming.
- Dedicated SLA tiers (P50/P95/P99 latency targets) and 99.9% uptime SLA.
- Routing & fallback v2 with policy engine and model-variant registry.
- Private installer (Terraform + operator) with KMS integration and audit-log forwarding.
- Console: per-route cost estimates, rollout UI improvements, and new dashboards.
Known issues:
- Extremely large context (>64k) workloads may experience degraded batching efficiency - mitigation planned in runtime K-scheduler follow-up.
- Initial Private installer supports AWS/Azure; GCP planned for next quarter.
post_release_actions:
- Monitor SLO dashboards for first 30 days; schedule daily review with SRE and product until stable.
- Customer success: proactive outreach to top 20 customers with migration recommendations.
- Engineering: prioritize runtime work-item to address large-context batching efficiency.
- Sales: updated pitch deck and pricing playbook distributed; enablement sessions scheduled.
